text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Joystick wire -> DevKitC-1 pin (left header J1)
Top button, one wire -> GPIO15 (J1 pin 8, internal pull-up)
Top button, other wire -> GND (J1 pin 22)
One END of every pot -> 3V3 (J1 pin 1) NEVER 5V!
Other END of every pot -> GND (J1 pin 22)
USB-C 'USB' port (native) -> PC: shows up as 'Falcon Pilot'

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Identify the unlabeled wires with a multimeter
Meter on resistance (20k range), joystick unplugged:
1. Find the 3 wires of one pot: two of them (the ENDS) read a fixed
value (typ. 5k or 10k) that does NOT change when you move the stick.
2. The 3rd wire is the WIPER: its reading to either end CHANGES as you
move one axis. The axis that changes it tells you X, Y or twist.
3. Button: continuity mode; the 2 wires that beep ONLY while the top
button is pressed. Either way round is fine.
4. Fewer wires than 11? Pots share a common END wire: it reads the
fixed value to the other ends of 2-3 pots. Wire it to GND or 3V3.
5. Which end goes to 3V3 vs GND doesn't matter. If an axis is backwards,
swap its two END wires (or set invert=true in config_pilot.h).
6. ~0 ohm / open only (no in-between)? It is a switch joystick, not
pots: wire each direction as a button to GND instead.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: the missing 74HC165s). Calibrate: hold the top button while plugging
in -> LED blue: move all axes to the ends, press -> yellow: let go,

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Wire colours are ROLES (red 3V3, black GND, yellow/green/blue wipers, brown button), not the colours of your joystick's wires.
